title: Investigations into the influence of fludarabine exposure on the outcome of patients after CAR-T cell therapy
summary:
Before therapy with CAR-T cells can be carried out, patients must be prepared for it with special drugs such as fludarabine. This drug is then excreted by the body, primarily via the kidneys. It is known that the amount of fludarabine in a patient's blood can vary considerably for the same dose. This is influenced by various factors, such as the individual function of the patient's kidneys. In this study, the amount of fludarabine in the blood of patients receiving CAR T-cell therapy will be measured at different time points. It will then be observed how often and to what extent typical side effects of CAR T-cell therapy occur, how well the therapy with CAR T-cells works and what correlation there is with the amount of fludarabine measured in the blood. In order to measure the effect of the therapy, we look at how the CAR-T cells have spread in the patient's blood at different points in time. This expansion of the CAR-T cells is routinely measured in the patient's blood at certain points in time after their administration. 
In addition, it will be checked whether the current reduction in the dose given to a patient with impaired kidney function leads to the desired amounts of fludarabine in the blood.
conditions: Multiple myeloma and malignant plasma cell neoplasms

interventions.name:
Adult, hospitalized patients of the participating clinics who are receiving CAR-T cell therapy for an aggressive B-cell lymphoma or multiple myeloma and whose lymphodepletion contains fludarabine are being investigated in this prospective intervention study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Adult, hospitalized patients of the participating clinics receiving CAR T- 
        cell therapy according to indication and whose conditioning plan 
        includes fludarabine
•	Diagnosis of multiple myeloma or aggressive B-cell lymphoma
•	Written consent of the patients
Exclusion criteria:
- Age < 18 years
- Lack of written consent of the patient
